content: Clomiphene is a medication prescribed to stimulate ovulation in women who do not produce eggs but wish to become pregnant. It belongs to a class of drugs known as ovulatory stimulants and mimics the action of estrogen, a hormone that promotes the development and release of eggs from the ovaries. Clomiphene is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically administered once daily for five days, starting on or around the fifth day of the menstrual cycle. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to take the medication at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not take more or less of the medication or use it more frequently than prescribed. In addition to its primary use, clomiphene is sometimes used to treat male infertility, menstrual irregularities, fibrocystic breast conditions, and persistent breast milk production. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your specific condition with your doctor. Clomiphene may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting clomiphene, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to clomiphene or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, ovarian cysts (other than those caused by polycystic ovary syndrome), uterine fibroids, abnormal vaginal bleeding, pituitary tumors, or thyroid or adrenal disorders. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking clomiphene, contact your doctor immediately. Be aware that clomiphene may cause blurred vision. Avoid driving or operating machinery, especially in low-light conditions, until you know how the medication affects you. Additionally, clomiphene increases the likelihood of multiple pregnancies (e.g., twins or more). Discuss the risks of multiple pregnancies with your doctor. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking clomiphene. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, contact your doctor for further instructions. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Clomiphene may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: flushing (a sensation of warmth), upset stomach, vomiting, breast discomfort, headache, or abnormal vaginal bleeding. Some side effects of clomiphene can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following: blurred vision, visual spots or flashes, double vision, stomach or lower abdominal pain, stomach swelling, weight gain, or shortness of breath. Long-term use of clomiphene may increase the risk of ovarian cancer, and it should not be used for more than six cycles. Discuss the risks of prolonged use with your doctor. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store clomiphene in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include upset stomach, vomiting, hot flashes, blurred vision, visual spots or flashes, blind spots, stomach swelling, and abdominal or lower abdominal pain. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order specific tests to monitor your body’s response to clomiphene. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
